reader.summary: During the week of October 17-24, 2026, Saudi Arabia endured its most intense Houthi attack campaign to date. Yemen's Houthis launched ballistic missiles and drones at multiple Saudi cities, killing at least three people at the Dammam airport and an Aramco oil field in the Eastern Region. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted several waves but could not stop all strikes. The United States ordered some embassy staff and diplomats to depart, and the United Kingdom deployed Typhoon fighter jets for defensive air patrols over Saudi cities. Aramco ordered the evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters and asked staff to work remotely. The kingdom postponed its flagship 'Davos in the Desert' investor conference to 2027, and airlines canceled or restricted flights to Riyadh. Egypt's President Sisi sought parliamentary authorization to provide military support to Saudi Arabia, with the vote delayed to October 26. Turkey moved to ratify the Mecca Defense Pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. Oil prices surged past $109 a barrel and Gulf stock markets fell. A Saudi helicopter crashed near the Yemen border, killing two troops. In a separate legal matter, a US judge ordered the detention of a Saudi engineer accused of bugging an OpenAI meeting room, with prosecutors claiming Saudi royal backing for the suspect.

display.eli5:
Yemen's Houthi rebels have been firing missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's cities and oil sites for weeks. This week they hit an airport and an oil field, killing people. Saudi Arabia is asking its neighbors and allies for help because its own air defenses caught most attacks but not all.

The Houthis are backed by Iran, and they want to show that Saudi Arabia is not safe. Saudi Arabia's economy depends on its oil exports, so every hit on an Aramco site or an airport shakes global markets and investor confidence.

Next week, two big things will happen. First, Egypt's parliament will vote to send troops to help defend Saudi Arabia, and Cairo will say exactly how many soldiers and what kind of equipment they are sending. Second, the Houthis will fire another big wave of missiles at a different Saudi city, and some people will get hurt. Aramco, the giant oil company, will also sign a deal to store some of its oil in another country so it is not all in one vulnerable place.

A real surprise would be Saudi Arabia announcing a huge new missile-defense purchase from France or the United States, or Iran and Saudi Arabia suddenly sitting down to talk directly. Either of those would change the whole picture of who is winning and who is losing.

history_used.HISTORY_BULLETINS:
Round 2026-10-17:
During the week of October 14 to 17, 2026, Saudi Arabia faced its most intense Houthi attack campaign to date. Iran-backed Yemeni rebels struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, the headquarters of oil giant Aramco, and multiple other locations with missiles and drones.
